evals.expected_output: A plan-only report: which remote branches are merged and would be deleted, which local worktrees are idle, which build/cache paths would be removed, and which open PRs would be driven. No branch, worktree, or file is actually deleted and no PR is touched.
expectations: Nothing is deleted — the working tree, worktree list, and remote branch list are identical before and after
Every candidate is listed with the reason it qualified (merged / idle / ignored artifact)
The report states explicitly that this was a dry run and names the command to run for real

evals.expected_output: Idle local worktrees are removed and build/cache artifacts deleted. Remote branches are untouched and no PR is driven, because --local-only scopes the sweep to the local checkout.
expectations: No remote branch is deleted and no PR is modified
A worktree containing uncommitted work is NOT removed — the work is rescued or the worktree is skipped with a reason
The summary distinguishes what was removed from what was deliberately skipped

evals.expected_output: The full sweep runs, but every destructive phase is confirmed with the user first. Merged remote branches, idle worktrees, and build artifacts are removed; open PRs are driven toward merge-ready.
expectations: The user is asked to confirm before the first destructive action, not after
An unmerged branch is never deleted without an explicit instruction naming it
The final report lists each phase with counts and anything skipped

evals.prompt: /cleanup in a checkout where the gh CLI is not installed
evals.expected_output: Fallback path. cleanup declares github_cli as an OPTIONAL capability, so the local half of the sweep (worktrees, build artifacts, local branches, reset-to-remote) still runs. The PR-driving and remote-branch phases are skipped with an explicit 'gh not available' message — never silently, and never by guessing at PR state from local refs.
expectations: The skill degrades rather than aborting: local cleanup completes
The skipped phases are named, with 'gh is not available' given as the reason
No attempt is made to infer merged-ness of remote PRs without gh
The report tells the user exactly what to re-run once gh is authenticated

evals.prompt: /cleanup on a repo whose worktrees contain uncommitted changes
evals.expected_output: Degraded, safety-first behavior. Uncommitted work is rescued (stashed or reported with its path) before any worktree is removed; a worktree whose work cannot be rescued is left in place and reported.
expectations: Each rescued or skipped worktree is named in the report with its dirty paths
The skill does not prompt-loop: it makes one decision per worktree and states it
